messages.subject: Error when starts compiling rjags model
parts:
Hello Ed,

Today I have a very simple question, that I believe is related to rjags. 

I've been running a very simple CFA model, and suddenly it tells me that I'm not passing the right object: 

"Compiling rjags model...
Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors"

If I try to fit the model using runjags or rjags the model runs fine. Do you have any idea if I'm doing something wrong of if the arguments of blavaan function have changed?

I'm attaching the dataset and you'll see my code and session info below. I'll appreciate any help you can give me.  


testData <- read.csv("testing.csv", na.string = "NA")


modCFA <- 'tsccAnx =~ tsccAnx1 + tsccAnx2 + tsccAnx3
           tscycAnx =~ tscycAnx1 + tscycAnx2 + tscycAnx3

          tsccDep =~ tsccDep1 + tsccDep2 + tsccDep3
          tscycDep  =~ tscycDep1 + tscycDep2 + tscycDep3

          tsccPTS =~ tsccPTS1 + tsccPTS2 + tsccPTS3

          tscycPTS =~ tscycIntru + tscycAvoid + tscycArousal

          tsccDis =~  tsccDis1 + tsccDis2 + tsccDis3
          tscycDis =~  tscycDis1 + tscycDis2 + tscycDis3

         tsccSC =~ tsccSc1 + tsccSc2 + tsccSc3
         tscycSC =~ tscycSc1 + tscycSc2 + tscycSc3

        tsccAnger =~  tsccAnger1 +  tsccAnger2 +  tsccAnger3
       tscycAnger =~  tscycAnger1 +  tscycAnger2 +  tscycAnger3

'


fitB1 <- bcfa(modCFA,
              data= testData,
              n.chains = 3,
              burnin=25000,
              sample=5000,
              target = "jags",
              bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
              mcmcfile = TRUE,
              do.fit = TRUE)

Esteban,

Thanks for the report. I reproduced this error once, then I think it went away when I upgraded to the newest version of lavaan (via the command below). But I was messing around during lavaan installation and can't be sure that this was it. Can you try and let me know if it solves the problem? Just in case you need it, the command is:

install.packages("lavaan", repos = "http://www.da.ugent.be", type = "source")

Ed

parts:
Esteban,

Upon further examination, it looks like the problem is the do.fit argument. If you remove that argument, the model seems to work (and you don't really need that argument, because the model will be estimated anyway). Nevertheless, I will fix it soon. I also just fixed some gradient warnings that popped up from the newer versions of lavaan.

Thanks for the example code!

Ed

Thanks for the example code!

Ed

Ed
